newsitem.title: USA: Clintons earn $1 million, give most to charity.
newsitem.headline: Clintons earn $1 million, give most to charity.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and his wife Hillary earned over $1 million last year according to documents released on Monday, with the $742,852 royalties from her book "It Takes A Village" dwarfing his $200,000 salary.

According to their 1996 tax return, which was made public by the White House, the Clintons had adjusted gross income of $1,065,101 in 1996, a huge leap from the $316,074 they earned the previous year.

Most of the rise reflected royalties from Mrs. Clinton's "It Takes A Village" book about child-rearing, whose proceeds after taxes and expenses were given to charity and accounted for the bulk of their $609,300 in charitable deductions.
The couple paid $205,667 in federal taxes but only owed $199,791, resulting in a refund of $5,876, which they chose to apply to their 1997 taxes. Last year the Clintons paid $75,437 in federal taxes.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters Clinton had met with his accountant on Monday and had noted he pays "a considerable amount" in taxes.

"He did say that he was proud that the first lady had been able to sell so many books and proud that she had been in a position to give the proceeds from those books to a number of very worthy charitable causes," McCurry added.

The return also showed a capital gain of $100,066 from the Boston Harbour Trust Co., taxable interest income of $28,606, dividend income of $5,141 and $2,214 in income attributed to taxable refunds, credits or offsets of state and local taxes.
The White House said the capital gains, as well as part of the interest and dividend income, were from Boston Harbour, the trustee of the Clintons' blind trust.
The return, signed by both Clintons, was dated April 14, 1997, one day before the tax deadline for most Americans.

Clinton's total salary, wages and tips came to $200,057, with the $57 reflecting royalties from an appearance he made on the Arsenio Hall television show in 1992. McCurry said that because of that income, Clinton had filed a California income tax return and owed $2 to the state.

The White House said Clinton filed a federal income tax return for Chelsea Clinton, his 17-year-old daughter, which showed income of $13,101 and tax of $1,969. Her income derives chiefly from the royalties from "Leading With My Heart," a memoir by her late paternal grandmother Virginia Kelly.

Asked if Clinton had said anything about how he felt about being a millionaire on paper, McCurry replied: "No, but I think some of you know that he's got some bills hanging around that probably diminshes his enthusiasm for that designation."
As of the end of 1996, Clinton had unpaid legal bills of more than $2.25 million from the Whitewater affair and other legal proceedings.

Separately, the White House said Vice President Al Gore and his wife Mary "Tipper" Gore had paid $80,941 in federal taxes for 1996 on adjusted gross income of $274,320. Gore's office said his salary as vice president is $171,500.

According to the Gores' income tax return, Mrs. Gore had 1996 net profit of $67,115 last year, chiefly from her work as an author and photographer. During the year she published a book of photographs and reminiscences entitled "Picture This."
